repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until(not ((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true))
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The candidate implements a periodic `if` check instead of a rising-edge wait. At t=100ms, the motion sensor was already true, but the candidate only evaluates the condition at the start of the 1000ms wrapper cycle, missing the rising edge that occurred before the first check. The IR requires blocking on the rising edge before executing the body.
diagnosis.change_summary: Changed the script to use a two-wait rearming pattern with `period` 1000. It first blocks until the motion sensor transitions to true (rising edge), then executes the body actions and the delay, and finally sets a flag to prevent re-firing until the sensor returns to false.
